This is the real factor. Engines are designed to have the right tolerances at operating temperature. When they're cold, the tolerances are finer and there's more friction. You want to compromise between making the engine do some work (so it warms up faster) and not revving it too high. So basically, if your driving conditions allow, you want to start driving as soon as your oil pressure is up to normal, but you want to keep your revs low until the engine is warm.
